module.description: System module definition for the lower kitchen corner shelf module.

parameterEffects.effect: corner_shelf_lower width changes carcass span, top/bottom panel width and drawer/front clear width.
corner_shelf_lower height changes side panels, front stack allocation and internal vertical clearances.
corner_shelf_lower depth changes side panel depth, drawer box depth and back panel footprint.
Board thickness changes panel stock thickness and all dependent internal clear dimensions.
Drawer count changes number of drawer fronts, runner sets and drawer box assemblies.
Drawer front heights redistribute the visible front stack and drawer aperture geometry.
Front gap changes revealed spacing between stacked fronts and side/top/bottom front edges.
Worktop thickness reduces effective carcass height when the module uses a worktop.
Plinth height changes support geometry and usable carcass height for floor-mounted modules.

notes: Generated from Arcigy liveRuntime.parts by the generic Revit import contract exporter.
The exported liveRuntime is normalized so the Revit family origin is at the module lower-left-bottom bounds.
Reference planes are generated before Revit geometry binding and are the controlling contract for imported board faces.
Each cabinet board/panel exports its own six face reference planes with part-specific names and colors.
Hardware such as legs, handles, hinges and clips stays as imported geometry and intentionally does not export reference planes.
Main lengthX and lengthZ dimensions use explicit ARCIGY_CTRL_LENGTH_X and ARCIGY_CTRL_LENGTH_Z control reference planes instead of depending on a particular board or kick face.
Low-module height and worktop thickness use explicit ARCIGY_CTRL_WORKTOP_TOP control reference planes when the app height is above the imported carcass geometry.
Corner depth uses explicit ARCIGY_CTRL_DEPTH_X and ARCIGY_CTRL_DEPTH_Z control reference planes so the main depth parameter is labeled directly, without inheriting small front geometry offsets.
Reference plane lines are local to their board face with a small visibility overrun instead of spanning the whole module.
Dimension labels are emitted only when the app runtime proves the measured span from numeric parameter values.
Semantic parameter-span dimensions bind position parameters such as depth, plinth setbacks and front gaps between existing board reference planes.
Shelf gap dimensions use generated shelfGap*Mm Revit length parameters derived from the app shelfGaps runtime array.
Compound runtime spans are documented for audit only; they are not emitted as extra ARCIGY_DIM_* driving labels because derived helpers overconstrain Revit families.

Plane-position dimensions are labeled only when they bind directly to a real Arcigy parameter; derived board positions are not exported as ARCIGY_POS helper parameters to avoid overconstraining Revit.

Control reference planes export as Strong Reference; board face reference planes export as Weak Reference so the Revit family has deterministic priority without making every board face a main family reference.
Coincident reference-plane locks are planned as a star from one primary reference plane per coincident group, not as all-pairs locks, to avoid avoidable overconstraint.

structuralCountContract.sourceRuntime: Maps dimension-group count parameters to the generated app-runtime parts they control. Count parameters are not length spans and must not be represented as invented Revit dimensions.

parameters.reason: This Arcigy parameter changes generated element cardinality in the app runtime. It is exported as a Revit number parameter and a structural-count contract, not as a fake length dimension label.

items.reason: This app parameter changes the number of generated elements, not a length span that can be FamilyLabel-bound to one Revit dimension.
